text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Greek Cypriot newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- The government will seek clarifications from the United States over comments by a U.S. Greek Cypriot lobbyist that the government asked for a postponement of the U.S. initiative on Cyprus.
- National Council meets today.
- Inquest rules that unknown assailants killed pro-Kurd activist Theofilos Georgiades.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Defence pact with Greece is unshakeable, says Greek Defence Minister Gerassimos Arsenis.
- Visiting MPs from Australia slam Turkey for its failure to talk peace.
- Government confirms outbreak of typhus fever in the Larnaca district.
HARAVGHI
- The government sought a postponement of the U.S. initiative on the Cyprus problem in April due to parliamentary elections on the island.
- The National Council is to meet today.
- Schools will work this year with a smaller number of assistant directors, while a shortage of classes still exists.
PHILELEPHTHEROS

- Fears are expressed that irresponsible persons are planning to retaliate against Turkish Cypriot workers and their Greek Cypriot employers after the murders of two Greek Cypriots by Turks last month.
- Democratic Kyprianou will run as a presidential candidate.
- Local businessman Nicos Shakolas plans to purchase the remaining 45 percent in Zako cosmetics and accessories outlet.
SIMERINI
- The defence pact with Greece is irreversible, says Greek defence minister.
- President Glafcos Clerides summons snap National Council meeting, without telling party leaders the agenda.
- New civil service positions will be created only in education and health in 1997.
